title: Reading and changing data
description:
Views read models with @Query. It fetches from the database and keeps the view up to date as data changes:

struct HabitList: View {
    @Query(sort: \Habit.createdAt) private var habits: [Habit]
    @Environment(\.modelContext) private var context

    var body: some View {
        List {
            ForEach(habits) { habit in
                Text(habit.name)
            }
            .onDelete { offsets in
                for index in offsets {
                    context.delete(habits[index])
                }
            }
        }
        .toolbar {
            Button("Add", systemImage: "plus") {
                context.insert(Habit(name: "New habit", symbol: "star"))
            }
        }
    }
}

The model context is your handle on the database: insert adds, delete removes. Changing a model's properties is just assignment: habit.name = "Read". SwiftData saves automatically.

Filter with a predicate, written as ordinary Swift:

@Query(filter: #Predicate<Habit> { $0.name.contains("Read") }, sort: \Habit.name)
private var readingHabits: [Habit]

For previews, use an in-memory container with sample data, so previews never touch your real database:

#Preview {
    HabitList()
        .modelContainer(for: Habit.self, inMemory: true)
}
instructions: Move your Habits project from its @Observable model to SwiftData: @Model classes, a model container, @Query in the list, and inserts and deletes through the model context. Make sure completions and streaks still work.
checklist: Habits and completions survive quitting the app.
The list uses @Query and stays up to date when I add, change or delete.

questions.question: How do you save a change to a model's property in SwiftData?

answers.text: Just assign it; SwiftData saves automatically

questions.why: Models are tracked by their context.

questions.question: Why give previews an in-memory container?

answers.text: So previews never change the real database

questions.why: Sample data stays in the preview.
